## a77893c9c05c

### Reproduced canonical-domain rejection and sampler omission

Audited generator SHA-256: `141c9e425a7dd8e624d2dd28c005d628e54b6046f09f773b4a74d349934d90c2`.

The selected Racket rule recognizes hollow rectangular frames with height and width at least 3. The generator's `self_check`, however, requires both dimensions to be at least 4. It rejects 2 of the 3 canonical pairs; each rejected pair contains two lawful 3×4 frames. A deterministic 200-draw probe found zero generated frames with any dimension 3; all sampled frame dimensions were at least 4×4. This is a reproduced canonical-support defect, not merely a stylistic mismatch.

`checks/audit/a77893c9c05c/input.json` is the first rejected canonical input. `self_check` returns two `frame should be at least 4x4` findings, while the selected Racket authority executes it successfully under rule hash `1152f803ad80`; see `checks/audit/a77893c9c05c/racket.json`. The combined audit preset also fails because the generator has no declared semantic contract or task tests.

Evidence: `checks/audit/a77893c9c05c/probe.json`, `checks/audit/a77893c9c05c/racket.json`, and `checks/audit/a77893c9c05c-combined/result.json`.

No source was changed. A repair should admit and sample height-3 or width-3 frames, add canonical acceptance tests, and declare a semantic contract distinguishing frame filling from bbox-filling distractor shortcuts.
